answer: Neighborhood curvature quota. Each agent gets a budget of introductions proportional to the local clustering coefficient of its transaction subgraph; dense honest clusters license more edges, sparse ones fewer. A clone farm needs real counterparties to raise its curvature, which means paying transaction fees and disclosing a lotus of shared timing across its members. The residual penetration hits a shale of unverified edges that reset to their nadir each epoch, forcing repeat spend. Attack cost scales with the square of farm size.
